chunks: Al-Saffar from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said:
When Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) finished with the people of Nahrawan, he said: 'After me, only those who are more entitled to the truth than he is will fight them.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.أَهْلِ اَلنَّهْرَوَانِ: The people of Nahrawan (referring to the Khawarij)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about fighting the Khawarij after his death?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) establishes a criterion for future legitimacy in fighting the Khawarij, asserting that any subsequent combatant must possess greater claim to the truth than his own. This statement underscores the high epistemological and spiritual status of Ali’s judgment during the Battle of Nahrawan, serving as a benchmark for valid authority in Shia political theology. It highlights that the right to lead the fight against rebels is not merely military but rooted in superior adherence to divine truth.
